cases.customer_question: Why did the RF report show Power Class 2 when the same module was expected to be Class 1?
question_variants: Why did the same module not appear as Class 1?
Was the RF test plan set to the wrong class?
Do we need to retest because the Bluetooth power class was wrong?
cases.actual_issue: The RF test plan was created with the wrong Power Class setting, causing the report to show Class 2 instead of the intended Class 1.
cases.plain_english_explanation: The product itself was not identified as the root problem. The test setup was configured incorrectly, so the report reflected the wrong power class. The measured result was still good enough to pass, but the evidence had to be corrected.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant acknowledged that the Class 2 result was caused by a test plan creation mistake. Because the measured result was at a level that could pass for both Class 1 and Class 2 coexistence, the practical correction was to rerun using the revised test plan and issue a corrected report.
cases.decision_logic: The reported RF Power Class depends on the test plan and declared test configuration. If the test plan uses the wrong Power Class, the report classification is unreliable even if the RF result itself passes.
cases.final_recommendation: Revise the test plan to Class 1, rerun the RF test, and issue a corrected report.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: The qualification evidence may show the wrong Power Class, causing customer dispute, report correction, retest, or qualification evidence inconsistency.
